test_title: PYST 7: Selection Post (Matric Level) - GA (Held On 31 Jul, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements about the All India Services (AIS) is correct?

options.text: All India Services officers can be transferred between states without the consent of the state governments.
The officers are recruited and controlled by the State Governments only.
The officers serve the Union Government exclusively.
The ultimate control lies with the Union Government.

solution:
The correct answer is __**All India Services officers can be transferred between states without the consent of the state governments.**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Article 312** of the **Constitution of India** empowers the **Parliament** to create **All India Services (AIS)** that are common to both the **Union** and the **States**.

• According to **Rule 6(1)** of the **IAS (Cadre) Rules, 1954**, while an officer is typically deputed with the concurrence of the **State Government**, the **Central Government** holds the overriding power. In any case of **disagreement** between the **Centre** and the **State**, the decision of the **Central Government** shall prevail, and the **State Government** must give effect to that decision. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***

• The officers of the **All India Services** are **recruited** and **appointed** by the **Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)** and the **President of India**, respectively. They are not recruited or controlled exclusively by **State Governments**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

• These officers serve both the **Union Government** and the **State Governments** on a **rotational basis** through a system of **deputation**. They do not serve the **Union** exclusively. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

• While the **Ultimate Control** regarding **disciplinary actions** and **removal** from service lies with the **Union Government**, the **Immediate Control** (such as **postings** and **transfers** within the state) lies with the **State Government**. ***Hence, statement 4 is partially correct but statement 1 is the most specific legal provision regarding inter-state transfers.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**, known as the **Iron Man of India**, is considered the **'Father of All India Services'** for his vision of a unified administrative structure to maintain the **integrity** of the **country**.

• The **Indian Forest Service (IFoS)** was established in the **year 1966** as the third **All India Service**, joining the **Indian Administrative Service (IAS)** and the **Indian Police Service (IPS)**.

• **Article 311** of the **Constitution** provides **protection** to civil servants against **arbitrary dismissal** or **reduction in rank**, ensuring they cannot be removed by an authority subordinate to their **appointing authority**.

• The **Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration (LBSNAA)**, located in **Mussoorie**, **Uttarakhand**, serves as the **training** ground for **IAS** officers, while **IPS** officers are trained at the **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy (SVPNPA)** in **Hyderabad**.

• The **All India Services Act, 1951** provides the legal framework for the **Government of India** to regulate the **recruitment** and **service conditions** of these officers.

**Important Points__**

• The **Cadre Allocation Policy** is designed to ensure that a **number** of officers in each **state cadre** come from outside that **state**, which helps in promoting **national integration** and preventing **parochialism**.

• The **Central Deputation Reserve (CDR)** is a specific **quota** that determines the **number** of officers from a **state cadre** who can be sent to serve in the **Union Government** at any given **time**.

• The **Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT)** under the **Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions** acts as the **cadre controlling authority** for the **IAS**.

• The **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)** is the **cadre controlling authority** for the **IPS**, while the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** controls the **IFoS**.
